result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers find the same core problems and propose similar Nunito-based fixes with preconnect, swap and fallback stacks. B is a little more thorough: it covers the clashing heading weights, correctly checks the #666 contrast and gives a responsive h1 size. It also warns that images or scripts may cause part of the slowness. Both miscount the font files (about 15 weights are requested, A says about 14 and B says about 18), but this doesn't change the conclusions. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers cover every rubric point: too many families, Lobster as body text at 13px with tight leading, hairline weights, the @import chain, display=block and missing fallbacks. Both suggest a friendly Nunito-based replacement. B is tighter and less repetitive (A covers unused weights twice and overstates the file count at about 18; the request is actually about 15). B also adds thoughtful touches like ui-rounded in the fallback stack and tabular-nums for prices and hours, while A's caveat about images and scripts is a nice touch of honesty.
